title: Collector caching + memoization for context bundles (incident + time window)
author: Jacob Stein
description: Motivation: During Phase 1 rollout we saw repeated context bundle requests in the first 5–10 minutes of an incident (auto-post + responders running `/incidentbot context` + retries when Slack transiently fails). Each request currently fans out to the same upstreams (release events, config snapshots, metrics queries). This creates avoidable load at exactly the wrong time and contributes to noisy latency for the bot. This PR adds a small, bounded memoization layer keyed by (incident_id, collector_id, region, window_start, window_end, mode) to reuse results within a short TTL and reduce upstream QPS. Approach: Add `CollectorCache` interface and default in-memory implementation with (1) async singleflight to prevent stampedes, (2) TTL per collector (deploy/config/metrics) with sane defaults, (3) size bounds + LRU eviction, and (4) explicit invalidation hooks when we know the data is stale. Cache only stores collector outputs that are already redacted / safe-to-post (same object the bundle renderer consumes); we do not cache raw upstream payloads. Restricted-mode is isolated via a separate cache namespace so restricted outputs are never reused for non-restricted incidents (and vice versa). Cache key details: `incident_id` (Slack thread ts or internal incident UUID), `collector_id` (deploy/config_diff/saturation/etc), `region` (or `global`), `window` (start/end rounded to collector granularity), `bundle_version` (to avoid cross-version reuse during rollouts), and `posting_mode` (normal vs restricted). Invalidation: (a) on incident state transitions (declared/resolved) we clear the incident namespace, (b) on a manual refresh command we bypass cache and then overwrite, (c) for deploy collector we additionally invalidate on new deploy event notification if present (best-effort), and (d) for config diff collector we invalidate on config snapshot version bump if available; otherwise TTL-driven. Performance notes/benchmarks: Local benchmark (recorded fixtures + simulated 3 collectors) shows first bundle assembly p95 unchanged (~1.3s) but repeated calls within TTL drop p95 to ~180–240ms (render + Slack formatting only). In staging with synthetic incident load (10 incidents, 3 responders spamming context every 30s), upstream calls to config snapshot endpoint reduced by ~78% and metrics backend queries reduced by ~64% over 15 minutes. Added logging for cache hit/miss rates by collector, and guardrails to fail open (cache errors never block collectors). Follow-ups: We should consider swapping the in-memory implementation for Redis in Private deployments if we need cross-replica reuse, but we should prove correctness first; this PR is scoped to per-process caching only.
commits: cache: introduce CollectorCache + in-memory singleflight implementation
collectors: thread cache through CollectorContext + memoize results by incident/window
cache: add bounded LRU + per-collector TTL config (with defaults)
commands: add /incidentbot context --refresh to bypass cache
observability: add cache hit/miss metrics + structured logs
tests: unit tests for keying, TTL expiry, singleflight, and invalidation hooks
changed_files: src/core/collector.ts (wiring: CollectorContext gains cache + key helpers)
src/collectors/deploy_collector.ts (cache key uses service/region + time window rounding)
src/collectors/config_diff_collector.ts (cache key includes config snapshot version when present)
src/collectors/saturation_collector.ts (TTL tuned shorter; avoids caching error responses)
docs/oncall.md (how caching works, when to refresh)
conversation: Rafael Mendes: This is the right direction. Two questions: (1) what happens when the cache entry is an error (upstream timeout)? We should avoid caching failures for long; otherwise responders keep seeing the same error even if the backend recovered. (2) Can we bound memory usage more explicitly? Incidents can get spammy.

Jacob Stein (author): Good catch. I updated behavior so we only cache successful collector results by default; errors are cached for 5s max to provide brief backoff and avoid stampedes. Also added max_entries + LRU eviction and a per-incident namespace cap (defaults to 128 entries).

Logan Wright: Please add metrics for cache hit/miss by collector and a counter for 'singleflight waiters' so we can tell if we're stampeding. Also: does the key include the rounded window? If responders run different window sizes we’ll have low hit rate.

Jacob Stein (author): Added `incidentbot_cache_hit_total{collector}` / miss / error, plus `incidentbot_cache_singleflight_waiters` gauge. Keying includes window_start/window_end rounded to collector granularity; for the default UX we always use the standard windows so it should hit. Custom windows will still miss, which is OK.
Marcus Lin: Security review: ensure restricted-mode cache cannot leak into normal mode. Also confirm we are not persisting any raw config snapshots / customer identifiers in cache.

Jacob Stein (author): Implemented separate namespaces for restricted vs normal and added a test to ensure keys never collide across modes. We cache only the post-redaction `CollectorOutput` (same object that gets rendered), and we do not store upstream payloads. Added a doc note + log fields scrubbed of customer IDs.

Sean Gallagher: From an on-call perspective, I want a clear way to force-refresh in Slack. The --refresh flag is good; can we document it in the incident bot usage doc and add a short hint in the error message when data is cached?
Jacob Stein (author): Added docs + a hint in the bundle footer when all collectors are served from cache (and a hint to run `/incidentbot context --refresh` if you suspect staleness).
Rafael Mendes: Approving. Please keep TTL defaults conservative for saturation since metrics lag is a thing; caching stale saturation snapshots could be misleading.
Jacob Stein (author): TTL for saturation set to 20s default with max 60s, and we avoid caching when the metrics backend indicates delayed samples. Added note in invalidation section.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Rafael Mendes; rollout behind existing feature flag (no behavior change unless collectors enabled).
